single-cell fragment inputs. Preserve the documented interval and
record-association behavior across general inputs; do not hard-code the public
fixture. Duplicate-policy and duplicate-CLI changes are not part of this task

# HMMRATAC and the meaning of an exclusion mask

This task uses the method described by Tarbell and Liu, “HMMRATAC: a Hidden Markov
Modeler for ATAC-seq,” *Nucleic Acids Research* 47(16), 2019.

- DOI: <https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkz533>
- Preprint: <https://doi.org/10.1101/306621>
- Offline project documentation: the supplied `source/README.md`,
  `source/MACS3/README.md`, HMMRATAC command implementation, and source comments
  are available in this snapshot.

The runtime is offline. The links above are provenance references; the intended
method facts needed for the task are summarized here.

## 1. What the analysis is trying to infer

ATAC-seq produces DNA fragments that reflect where chromatin is physically
accessible to the transposase. A peak caller turns those fragments into genomic
regions that are likely to be open chromatin. Those regions are often used later
to study regulatory elements, cell identity, and changes between conditions.

The input is not just a list of independent points. Each paired-end fragment has
two coordinates and a length. In single-cell fragment files it also has a barcode
and a count. These details are part of the scientific observation.

## Repair summary

**Defect.** In `hmmratac_cmd.run`, the exclusion mask was read into `blacklist_regions` but only applied to *training/candidate regions* (after EM). The fragment `petrack` that feeds EM, `count_fraglengths`, `generate_digested_signals`, and `pileup_bdg` was never filtered. So masked fragments leaked into the model population, distorting the learned fragment-length distributions and derived signals on **every** chromosome — including ones the mask doesn't cover.

**Fix.** Apply the mask at the observation level, before EM, so masked fragments never enter the learned population.

- `source/MACS3/Signal/PairedEndTrack.py`: added a module-level `_blacklist_survivor_mask` helper plus a `filter_blacklist` method on both `PETrackI` (paired-end) and `PETrackII` (count/barcode). Each removes fragments whose `[l, r)` overlaps any mask `[bs, be)` using half-open semantics (`l < be and r > bs`), recomputes `total`/`length`/`average_template_length` from survivors, keeps `PETrackII` counts and barcodes aligned, preserves record multiplicity, and drops chromosomes that become fully masked.
- `source/MACS3/Commands/hmmratac_cmd.py:142`: calls `petrack.filter_blacklist(blacklist_regions.regions)` right after the blacklist is parsed, before the EM stage. The existing region-level `exclude` calls for training/candidate regions are left intact.

**Verification.**
- `python reproduce.py` → `status: consistent`, exit 0 (both BEDPE/PETrackI and FRAG/PETrackII paths).
- Edge cases confirmed directly: half-open boundaries (fragment ending at mask start and starting at mask end survive), overlapping/adjacent masks, fully-masked chromosome dropping out, and duplicate coordinate records kept/removed together with counts and barcodes intact.
- The pre-existing `count_fraglengths`/`fraglengths` upstream quirks (called out in `bench_probe.py` as out of scope) are untouched, and no duplicate flags or policy were changed.

The fix is general (no hard-coded fixture values) and covers all HMMRATAC input formats since BAMPE/BEDPE build `PETrackI` and FRAG builds `PETrackII`.
